tag_field: labels (array of label names); alternatives: body (markdown text), issue_field_values (org-owned repos with issue fields enabled only)
tag_visible_to_end_users: yes (labels and body are shown on the issue; no hidden metadata field exists on issues)
exact_lookup: exact (List repository issues takes a 'labels' filter of comma-separated label names; issue_field_values also has a field_slug:value filter. Body text can only be found through Search issues, which is keyword search)
reversible: partial (REST can only close an issue: PATCH state=closed, state_reason=not_planned/duplicate. Deleting needs the GraphQL deleteIssue mutation)
notes: Labels are silently dropped unless the caller has push access. The docs do not say whether a label name that does not exist yet gets created, so create the label first with POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels. One label per operation also fills up the repo's label list.

tag_field: labels (comma-separated names; the docs say new labels are created if needed); alternative: description
exact_lookup: exact (List project issues 'labels' filter: issues must have all the given labels to be returned. The 'search' parameter over title/description is keyword search)
reversible: yes (DELETE /projects/:id/issues/:issue_iid; Planner/Owner roles can delete any issue, other members only issues they authored)
notes: The docs say no labels are needed up front because labels are created on create. The created_at override needs admin or owner rights, and no idempotency key is documented.

api: Jira Cloud REST v3 - Create issue (POST /rest/api/3/issue)
tag_field: properties (issue entity properties set atomically at create through the IssueUpdateDetails 'properties' array, key/value, max 32768 bytes). Visible alternatives: labels or a custom text field in 'fields'
tag_visible_to_end_users: no for issue properties (an API-only store; the docs do not describe any UI display). Yes for labels and custom fields
exact_lookup: search (JQL has exact operators such as labels = x or a custom field, but /rest/api/3/search/jql says 'Recent updates might not be immediately visible'. reconcileIssues only gives read-after-write for issue ids you already know, max 50. Issue properties are JQL-searchable only when a Connect jiraEntityProperties or Forge jira:entityProperty module indexes them. No lag figure is stated)
reversible: yes (DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}, needs the Delete issues permission; deleteSubtasks for issues with subtasks)
notes: The best hidden tag is an issue property written in the same create call. A plain REST client can't look it up without an app-defined index, and labels and custom fields depend on the eventually consistent JQL search.
sources: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json (official v3 OpenAPI: POST /rest/api/3/issue, IssueUpdateDetails, DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}, GET /rest/api/3/search/jql)

native_key: partial (IssueCreateInput.id: 'The identifier in UUID v4 format. If none is provided, the backend will generate one.' The client can pick the primary key, but the docs do not say what a retry with the same id does, such as an error versus returning the existing issue. There is no idempotency key or retention window for issues; idempotencyKey exists only for OAuth application creation)
tag_field: id (client-supplied UUID v4 primary key). Alternatives: description, labelIds
tag_visible_to_end_users: unclear (the docs do not say whether the UUID appears in the UI; users normally see team identifiers such as 'LIN-123')
exact_lookup: exact (query issue(id: String!) 'looked up by its unique identifier'; IssueFilter also has an id comparator)
reversible: yes (issueDelete trashes the issue with a 30-day grace period, with permanentlyDelete for admins only; issueArchive)
notes: This is the closest to a native key in the set, since a client-chosen UUID makes a retry detectable through issue(id:). Server-side dedup of a duplicate create is not documented, so it stays out of class K.
sources: https://github.com/linear/linear/blob/master/packages/sdk/src/schema.graphql (official Linear SDK schema: IssueCreateInput, issueCreate, issue, issueDelete, issueArchive)

tag_field: external.gid (plus external.data). App-specific custom external data accepted in the TaskCreateRequest body; gid up to 1,024 chars, data up to 32,768 chars
tag_visible_to_end_users: no ('These fields are not visible in the UI'; only the same OAuth app can see them)
exact_lookup: exact (after setting an external gid, 'external:custom_gid' can be used anywhere an object gid is accepted, e.g. GET /tasks/external:<gid>)
reversible: yes (DELETE /tasks/{task_gid} moves the task to the requester's trash, recoverable for 30 days)
notes: external needs OAuth because it is app-specific, so it is unavailable with a personal access token. The docs do not state whether external gids must be unique.
sources: https://github.com/Asana/openapi/blob/master/defs/asana_oas.yaml (official Asana OpenAPI: POST /tasks TaskCreateRequest incl. 'external', DELETE /tasks/{task_gid})

api: Trello REST - Create a new card (POST /1/cards)
tag_field: desc (or name). Custom fields and pluginData are not create parameters; custom fields need a separate call after create
exact_lookup: search (GET /1/search full-text 'query', no freshness or lag guarantee stated). Otherwise list_only by listing the cards on a list or board (GET /1/lists/{id}/cards and /1/boards/{id}/cards have no field filters)
notes: No idempotency mechanism appears anywhere in the Trello OpenAPI spec. A hidden tag would need a separate custom-field write after create, which is not atomic.

api: Notion - Create a page (POST /v1/pages) with a data source (database) parent
tag_field: a rich_text (or other text) property in 'properties' of a data-source page. A page parented by another page can only carry 'title'
tag_visible_to_end_users: yes (the property is part of the database schema and appears as page/database properties; the API docs offer no hidden metadata field)
exact_lookup: exact (POST /v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}/query with filter rich_text.equals 'matches the provided string'; up to 10,000 results per query; case sensitivity not stated)
reversible: partial (PATCH the page with in_trash=true, restorable with in_trash=false; 'The API does not support permanently deleting pages')
notes: This works only when the page is created in a data source whose schema has a text property reserved for the operation id. The query endpoint can return 503 on datastore timeouts.

api: Confluence Cloud REST v2 - Create page (POST /wiki/api/v2/pages)
tag_field: title (the only free-form field set atomically besides body). Hidden option: content property via POST /wiki/api/v2/pages/{id}/properties, which is a separate post-create call and not atomic. Labels also need a separate call
tag_visible_to_end_users: yes for title and body. No for content properties (API-accessible app/entity data)
exact_lookup: exact (CQL title = "..." is documented as an exact match, '~' is fuzzy, and label = is exact; GET /pages and /spaces/{id}/pages take a 'title' filter whose exactness the docs do not state. Content properties are CQL-searchable only when a Connect confluenceContentProperties module indexes them. Search-index freshness is not documented)
reversible: yes (DELETE /wiki/api/v2/pages/{id} moves the page to trash; purge is available)
notes: An exact lookup needs the op id in the visible title. The hidden content-property route is neither atomic with create nor queryable without an app index. The v2 spec does not say whether titles must be unique within a space, so duplicate-title rejection is unclear.
sources: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/openapi-v2.v3.json (official v2 OpenAPI: POST /pages, GET /pages title filter, DELETE /pages/{id}, /pages/{page-id}/properties)

api: Bitbucket Cloud REST - Create a comment on a pull request (POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/comments)
exact_lookup: exact (List PR comments supports the q filter language: content.raw = "..." for equality or content.raw ~ "..." for case-insensitive substring)
notes: The PR comment endpoint was examined because the current Bitbucket Cloud OpenAPI spec has no /issues paths. The intro page still lists /issues among filterable endpoints, so issue-tracker availability is unclear. The comment schema has no hidden metadata field.

api: Azure DevOps REST 7.1 - Work Items - Create (POST {org}/{project}/_apis/wit/workitems/${type})
tag_field: a custom string field (Custom.<Name>) added to an inherited process and hidden from the form layout ('Hide from layout'), set via JSON Patch /fields/Custom.<Name>. Visible alternative: System.Tags
tag_visible_to_end_users: no if the custom field is hidden from the layout (the data stays in the store). Tags are visible on forms by default
exact_lookup: exact (WIQL via POST _apis/wit/wiql: [Custom.<Name>] = 'value'; the docs only say '=' operators 'work as expected' and do not state case sensitivity. Tags support only Contains / Does Not Contain, and whether that matches whole tags or substrings is not stated)
reversible: yes (DELETE .../wit/workitems/{id} moves the item to the Recycle Bin; destroy=true deletes permanently)
notes: The hidden custom field needs Project Collection Administrator rights on the process, done once per org. validateOnly=true is a dry run, not dedup.

tag_field: column_values (a Text or Long Text column reserved for the op id)
tag_visible_to_end_users: yes (columns are part of the board; the docs offer no hidden metadata field)
exact_lookup: exact (items_page_by_column_values: Text is a 'case-insensitive match of the entire text value', Long Text an 'exact match of the entire text value'; limit up to 500)
notes: The board needs a dedicated text column. The docs say nothing about consistency or lag for items_page_by_column_values.

tag_field: custom_fields (a Text custom field set in the create body). Alternatives: tags, description/markdown_content
tag_visible_to_end_users: yes (custom fields show on tasks; the API docs describe no hidden variant)
exact_lookup: exact (Get Tasks and Get Filtered Team Tasks accept a custom_fields filter; '==' is 'exact match for text Custom Fields', while '=' is a fuzzy contains)
reversible: yes (DELETE /api/v2/task/{task_id} 'Delete a task from your Workspace')
notes: Use the '==' operator, because '=' on text fields is documented as a fuzzy contains match. custom_item_id is a task-type id, not an external id.
